$comment: NEON LINK hero numerals — the tempo readout on the 128x128 panel. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §4 asks for 24-32px tall digits and open decision §15.1 asked which font. Answer: a purpose-built seven-segment set. The 5x7 UI font scaled 3x tops out at 21px and reads as blown-up text; a segment readout reads as an instrument, is crisp by construction at 1-bit, and only needs the 13 glyphs a tempo can contain.
$source_of_truth: A segment font's real source is its segment map, not a pixel grid. Edit the geometry or the per-glyph segment lists here and run scripts/gen_design.py; review the result in design/fonts/hero_preview.txt, which is regenerated alongside the packed header and checked in.

segments.$comment: Standard seven-segment naming. Vertical segments overlap the horizontal ones by the stroke width so the joins are square and solid with no notch at the corners.

$tracking_comment: Pixels between glyph cells. '120.0' measures 16+2+16+2+16+2+6+2+16 = 78px, which centres on 128 with room to spare, and '--.-' during startup keeps the same optical weight.
